#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=dr5-rep-tf
#SBATCH --output=dr5-rep-tf_%A.log
#SBATCH --mem=0
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=24
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --no-requeue
#SBATCH --time=23:00:00
#SBATCH --constraint=A100
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH --exclude=compute-0-7,compute-0-5

# Train Zoobot (tensorflow version) on DR5 shards from scratch on Slurm cluster.
# You will need to adjust various paths
# Run with sbatch replication/replicate.sh

pwd; hostname; date

nvidia-smi

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:/share/apps/cudnn_8_1_0/cuda/lib64

ZOOBOT_DIR=/share/nas2/walml/repos/zoobot
PYTHON=/share/nas2/walml/miniconda3/envs/zoobot/bin/python

# make these with shards_sbatch
# W+22a originally trained with validation data from an automatic subset of the train data,
# so there's no explictly-known validation set
TFRECORD_DIR=/share/nas2/walml/repos/gz-decals-classifiers/data/decals/shards/all_2p5_unfiltered_n2
TRAIN_DIR=$TFRECORD_DIR/train_shards
TEST_DIR=$TFRECORD_DIR/eval_shards

THIS_DIR=/share/nas2/walml/repos/gz-decals-classifiers

EXPERIMENT_DIR=$THIS_DIR/results/tensorflow/dr5/efficientnet_dr5_tensorflow_greyscale

$PYTHON $ZOOBOT_DIR/zoobot/tensorflow/examples/train_model_on_shards.py \
    --experiment-dir $EXPERIMENT_DIR \
    --shard-img-size 300 \
    --resize-size 224 \
    --train-dir $TRAIN_DIR \
    --test-dir $TEST_DIR \
    --epochs 200 \
    --batch-size 512 \
    --gpus 2  \
    --wandb


# you might make (see shards.sh) and then train on some very small shards to debug everything first

# TRAIN_DIR=$ZOOBOT_DIR/data/decals/shards/decals_debug/train_shards
# EVAL_DIR=$ZOOBOT_DIR/data/decals/shards/decals_debug/eval_shards

# EXPERIMENT_DIR=$THIS_DIR/results/decals_debug

# python $ZOOBOT_DIR/train_model.py \
#     --experiment-dir $EXPERIMENT_DIR \
#     --shard-img-size 32 \
#     --resize-size 224 \
#     --train-dir $TRAIN_DIR \
#     --eval-dir $EVAL_DIR \
#     --epochs 2 \
#     --batch-size 8

reasons: The script requests a node with an A100 GPU using `--constraint=A100` but does not explicitly request any GPUs for the job using a directive like `--gpus`, `--gpus-per-task`, or `--gres`.

There is a resource mismatch: the application is launched with `--gpus 2`, indicating a need for two GPUs, but the Slurm job has not been allocated any. This will likely cause the application to fail at runtime.
issues: To fix the GPU allocation issue, add a Slurm directive to request the two GPUs, for example: `#SBATCH --gpus=2` or `#SBATCH --gres=gpu:A100:2`.

Paths to the Python executable, libraries, and data directories are hardcoded. This makes the script less portable. Using environment modules for software (like CUDA and Python) and relative paths or environment variables for data is recommended.

The script sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` manually. This can be fragile and may conflict with system-managed environments. Using an environment module system (e.g., `module load cuda cudnn`) is generally a more robust practice.
